shorts.title: What you will learn: Pointer arithmetic
shorts.hook: P plus one does not add one byte.
shorts.script: P plus one does not add one byte. Today we do maths with addresses. The rules are simple, but they surprise most beginners. When you add one to a pointer, it moves by one item, not by one byte. For an int pointer, the address grows by four. For a double pointer, it grows by eight. You may subtract two pointers into the same array. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: What you will learn: Pointer arithmetic.

shorts.title: Pointer arithmetic in one minute
shorts.hook: When you add one to a pointer
shorts.script: When you add one to a pointer, it moves by one item, not by one byte. For an int pointer, the address grows by four. For a double pointer, it grows by eight. You may subtract two pointers into the same array. You get the number of items between them. You may not add two pointers. Think of a bus conductor. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Pointer arithmetic in one minute.

shorts.title: Inside the second program
shorts.hook: Start points to the first item.
shorts.script: Start points to the first item. End points right after the last item. The difference is five. That is the number of items. End minus one points to the last item. It reads five. This idea powers many library functions. The program prints five and five. P plus one moves by one item. The compiler scales the step by the size of the type. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Inside the second program.

shorts.title: Bug of the Day: Adding two pointers
shorts.hook: Can you spot the bug in pointer arithmetic?
shorts.script: Can you spot the bug in pointer arithmetic? Bug of the Day. We add two pointers to find the middle. The compiler says invalid operands to binary plus. The sum of two addresses has no meaning. Take the distance between them, halve it, and add it to the low pointer. The sum of two addresses has no meaning. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Bug of the Day: Adding two pointers.

shorts.script: Can you print an array backwards with a pointer in pointer arithmetic? A pointer asked for directions. The answer was, just add one. Use a pointer that starts at the last item.
